correctness.rationale: Independently evaluated all seven norms for x=(1,1), y=(1,-1), z=(-1,4i/3). The signed gap is exactly 2/3[3*2^(1/p)+(3^p+4^p)^(1/p)-8], strictly decreasing in p; elementary rational fourth/cube root inequalities bracket its unique zero between 3 and 4; its infinity value is -2/3. The phase is optimal at +/-i by equality in Cauchy-Schwarz for |1+te^(iθ)|+|-1+te^(iθ)|. The real n=3 sign triple has gap 4*3^(1/p)-6<0 for p>q, while all real normed planes obey HH via zonoid representation; a one-coordinate complex norm is the real Euclidean plane. Zero padding proves the all-n statement. Independent checker confirms nine finite/infinity exponents and phase slices. Threshold q is only exact for this witness, NOT a universal optimal p threshold.
residual_risks: Classical planar zonoid theorem is used as a standard external structural lemma; individual complex p values are only corroboration.
No global complex exponent threshold below q is established.

value.rationale: Minimum scalar-coordinate obstruction is a natural sharp geometric dimension invariant over an entire open exponent interval, and its dependence on R versus C is structural. Explicit Pythagorean imaginary phase explains the failure of the usual planar protection; fixed-amplitude optimizing lemma makes the obstruction robust rather than a single unmotivated numerical instance. The work does not claim the first complex failure exponent or a general Banach-space characterization.
residual_risks: The novelty is narrow to the complex 2-coordinate obstruction; real-plane and real 3-coordinate results were already known.

final_claim: For every p greater than the unique q in (3,4) with 3*2^(1/q)+(3^q+4^q)^(1/q)=8, Hornich-Hlawka fails in complex l_p^n exactly when n>=2 and in real l_p^n exactly when n>=3; a specified complex two-coordinate 3-4-5 witness has exact threshold q and imaginary phase is minimizing among fixed-modulus phases.
limitations: Every p in (q,infinity] and all finite n; q itself has zero gap only for this witness.
Global p onset for complex l_p^2 and all amplitudes/phases is not determined.
